status: PROPOSAL - a mission-map data instance for the optional tactical layer (issue #515), validated by strategy_game/mission_map.py. No rule, cost, action economy, damage, initiative or difficulty lives anywhere in this file. Walkability is the only spatial property asserted here; what an agent may DO on the map awaits author-approved core mechanics.
sources: issue #515: 'Prototype a small (~20x20) top-down map with walls, doors, four selectable characters, click-to-move and pathfinding'
issue #515: 'One reusable tile-based mission environment supporting exploration, dialogue, clues, hacking, PSI, stealth and combat'
issue #515: 'Reuse NooPunk's existing lightweight Fate-inspired stats, tags, actions, wounds and mission consequences wherever feasible; avoid inventing a second full ruleset'
issue #515 non-goals: no complex animation, no 3D, no giant maps, no sophisticated enemy AI, no mandatory combat in the first iteration
docs/design/ISSUE_515_TACTICAL_MAP_SPIKE.md (sibling groundwork): renderer comparison, cross-layer contracts, milestone list, municipal-archive acceptance scenario

strategy_game/map_spec.py is the STRATEGIC location graph (8 playable nodes, reachability only) and explicitly 'not a map renderer and not a movement system'; this file is the tactical grid it deliberately did not provide
strategy_game/data/connectivity.json + strategy_game/cyber.py own network reachability and eras (issue #344); a floor plan here never asserts network reachability

provenance.note: the schema and this instance are this session's work; the renderer choice and every gameplay rule remain the author's

consumes.strategic_map: strategy_game/map_spec.py owns the strategic node/route graph. This tactical grid does not replace it: a mission takes place inside ONE strategic location.
consumes.network_reachability: strategy_game/cyber.py owns whether a network path exists in the current era. A terminal on this map is a physical fact; whether it can reach anything is decided there.
consumes.roster: the five-seat faction roster (one leader + four agents). Four agents deploy here; the leader does not appear as a fifth squad slot.
consumes.provenance: strategy_game/provenance.py owns the provenance vocabulary for outcomes.

grid.note: 20x20 is the prototype target #515 names, not a universal size rule.

#.name: wall
#.note: blocks movement and blocks any path through the cell

+.name: door
+.note: walkable only if a door record for this cell declares state 'open'

T.name: terminal
T.note: a workstation occupies the cell; it is operated from an adjacent cell

P.name: person
P.note: conversed with from an adjacent cell

o.name: obstacle
o.note: furniture or clutter; no rule attaches to it

X.name: exit
X.note: the mission boundary; entering it is an intent the resolver adjudicates, not a transition this schema performs

doors.note: records room; the only door, so a closed state would seal the room

interactables.label: night caretaker
interactables.note: the conversation route into the case; knows the access policy

interactables.label: public catalogue terminal
interactables.note: reachability of anything behind it is decided by cyber.py in the current era

interactables.label: transfer log
interactables.note: the clue that does not require the conversation

objectives.note: one noncombat route to the case

overlays.note: display-only impression near the microfiche; it grants no access and does not change walkability
display-only marker of a networked device

what_this_is_not: not a movement system: path() reports which cells a route crosses, never what it costs or whether the agent may take it
not a combat map: no cover, line of sight, initiative, hit points or damage is modelled
not a rules engine: no difficulty, modifier, action point or turn structure appears here
not a network map: a terminal's reachability belongs to cyber.py and the current era
not canonical: a proposal for author review under issue #515
